call_points.text: FY27 wire rope volume growth guided at 10-12%, including the Middle East at current levels.
Value growth guided at ~15% for FY27, with volume growth continuing at similar levels in coming years.
India Ratings upgraded long-term rating to IND AA- from IND A+ with stable outlook.
Operating margin floor raised to a minimum of 20%, from the earlier 18-19% band.
Order book not quantified; management says visibility for the next six months and 85% of business is replacement market.
Analyst pressed on why margins would fall from 22% to 20%; management said 22% is not a straight-line benchmark.
Plasticated LRPC approvals expected in weeks; current output 2,500 tons, targeted to double to 4,000-4,500 tons.
Thailand plant modernisation to show significant improvement over the next 18 months, adding specialised cords and elevator ropes.

penalties.details: The Company has been convicted under section 241 of Cr.P.C. for the offence under Rule 58 of Mineral Conservation and Development Rules, 1988, read with section 21(2) of Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 for violation of Rule 13(3) of Mineral Conservation and Development Rules, 1988 and has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs. 50,000/-.
penalties.impact: There is no financial or operational impact on the activties of the company since the amount is immaterial. The Company has paid the fine and the matter has been disposed off.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Last Disclosure made on 8th September 2023: An order passed for confirmation of penalty of Rs. 11,65,184/- by the Assistant Commissioner of State (Audit), Punjab Revisional Authority for Erroneous claim of Input Tax Credit.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of State (Audit), Punjab Revisional Authority
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal before the GSTAT against the order levying demand. The said appeal is pending for disposal.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Last disclosure made vide Integrated Governance filing for the quarter ended 30th September 2025: The Deputy Commissioner passed an order and dismissed the appeal filed by the company due to non-deposit of pre-deposit of additional demand required to entertain the appeal. The Company has duly paid the pre-deposit to contest the appeal and has accordingly challenged the order of Deputy Commissioner by filing appropriate appeal before the Tribunal.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Excise and Taxation Officer – cum State Tax Officer, Hoshiarpur – Ward No. 3
tax_litigation.status: The Company has opted for settlement of this matter under the OTS scheme introduced by the Punjab Government. As per the OTS scheme, there was full waiver of interest and penalty. Further, there was slab wise tax rebate also on the tax amount. After due consideration of the facts and legal position, the Company decided to settle the matter under the OTS scheme and has received OTS-4 also after due payment of applicable tax.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Last Disclosure made on 5th February 2025: Order passed by the Commissioner of CGST & CX, Jamshedpur, imposing a penalty of Rs. 7,14,46,604/- under relevant provisions of Finance Act, 1994 read with relevant provisions of CGST Act, 2017 on allegation of Non payment of Service Tax on Royalty pertaining to the period April 2016 to June 2017.
tax_litigation.status: The CESTAT has passed a final Order in the matter concerning Service Tax on royalty payments made under the mining lease wherein they have deleted the demand on account of service tax on royalty and consequential penalty on it.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Last Disclosure made on 6th February 2025: Order has been issued by the Assistant Commissioner of CGST & CX, Division III, Jamshedpur, imposing a penalty of Rs. 1,93,10,080/- under relevant provisions of the CGST Act 2017 read with IGST Act 2017 on account of irregular claim of Input Tax Credit pertaining to the period of July 2017 to March 2019.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of CGST & CX, Division III, Jamshedpur
tax_litigation.status: The Company has received an Order-in-Appeal, passed by the Commissioner (Appeals), Ranchi, allowing the Company's appeal and setting aside the Order-in-Original in its entirety.

operating_notes.text: FY26 revenue grew 6.2% to ₹3,691.1 Cr with operating EBITDA at ₹705.1 Cr.
Rope capacity is about 140,000 tons at 75% utilisation; wires 80,000 tons at 75-78%; LRPC about 60,000 tons plus 6,000 tons plasticated at about 70%.
LPG and propane costs rose to ₹120,000-130,000 per ton from ₹60,000, adding ₹2.5-3 Cr a month, with 25% of requirement shifting to natural gas.
International revenue is 57% of topline; Europe about 26% and the US 9%, with US market share below 5%.
Value-added rope share rose to 73% of the wire rope business in Q1FY27 from 70% in FY26, supporting EBITDA per tonne of ₹40,581.
Realisation per tonne in Q1FY27: wires ~₹85,000, blended LRPC ~₹79,000, domestic rope ~₹1,90,000 and international rope ~₹3,70,000-3,80,000.
Middle East is ~9% of revenue; India holds 65-70% rope market share, 60-65% in elevator ropes and over 95% in ports.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹979.26 Cr (+9.3% YoY), net profit ₹148.03 Cr (+46.7% YoY).
On April 30, 2026, Usha Martin announced Q4FY26 revenue of ₹979.3 Cr and PAT of ₹148.0 Cr.
On 8 May 2026, Usha Martin filed the transcript of its Q4 & FY26 earnings call, where management guided to a minimum 20% operating margin and 10-12% volume growth, with ₹300 Cr capex over two years.
Rajeev Jhawar, as Promoter, confirmed no encumbrance on Usha Martin shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) on April 7, 2026.
Q1FY27 (Jul 2026): Revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹1,033 Cr, EBITDA margin 20.1%, PAT ₹142 Cr; India Ratings upgraded to IND AA-; net cash ~₹465 Cr.
Usha Martin completed the transfer of U M Cables Limited's business undertaking to R R Kabel via slump sale on October 31, 2026.

watchlist.text: Dividend approval by shareholders at the ensuing AGM
Ratification of Cost Auditor remuneration by shareholders

watchlist.response: Rope volume grew about 5%; Middle East conflict cost about 900 tons, without which growth would have been about 8%.
watchlist.text: Volume growth lagging despite strong margins

watchlist.response: Declined to quantify, citing only six months of visibility and 85% replacement-market share.
Said 22% is not a straight-line benchmark; 20% is the minimum floor and mix can move it.
watchlist.text: Why margins would fall from 22% to 20%
Plasticated LRPC customer approval paperwork (verbal confirmation received)

watchlist.response: Middle East down ~28% (~1,000 tonnes); India, US and Europe grew, and the inquiry pipeline supports the guidance.
watchlist.text: Wire rope volumes flat for three quarters despite 10-12% FY27 guidance; how will the gap close?

watchlist.response: Only the absolute steel increase is passed through; a 13% steel rise does not translate to 13% on rope prices. 20% margin floor maintained.
watchlist.text: Steel prices up ~13% QoQ but EBITDA per tonne up only ~3% QoQ; margin contracted sequentially.

watchlist.response: Verbal confirmation received from a global customer; paperwork delayed but progressing.
watchlist.text: Plasticated LRPC approvals promised 'within weeks' in the Q4 call; have they come?

watchlist.response: Cables is non-core and under review for alternative use; Thailand plan expected in 6 months.

status_history.evidence: Business undertaking of U M Cables Limited transferred to R R Kabel Limited via slump sale effective 31st October 2026.

watchlist.text: U M Cables loss-making and Thailand PAT negative; turnaround plan?
